sections.title: What TypeScript is

blocks.title: Not from your PDFs
blocks.text: Your PDFs do not cover this topic, so this page was written for the site. Your 12-week plan lists React, hooks, rendering, performance, state management and TypeScript. Check it against the official documentation, or give me a PDF to replace it.

blocks: TypeScript is JavaScript plus a compile-time type checker. The types are erased: nothing about them exists at run time, much like Java generics. **A value from your API is whatever the server sent**, whatever type you wrote for it.

sections.title: Structural typing: the big difference from Java
blocks: Java is nominal: a class matches an interface only if it says `implements`. TypeScript is structural: anything with the right shape matches.

sections.title: Narrowing and discriminated unions
blocks: The compiler follows your checks. A **discriminated union** makes impossible states impossible to write, and it is the most useful pattern in React code.

blocks.title: One type instead of three flags
Gotcha
blocks.text: `any` switches the checker off and spreads silently. Use `unknown` for values you have not checked: the compiler then forces you to narrow before use. `response.json()` returns `any`, so annotating it does not validate it. Use a schema library such as Zod where bad data would hurt.

blocks.title: Interview angle
blocks.text: **How is TypeScript's type system different from Java's?** It is structural rather than nominal, types are fully erased at run time so there is no `instanceof` for interfaces, and it has unions, literal types and flow-based narrowing, which let you model states precisely.

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
- Types are erased: they do not validate API responses.
- Structural typing: shape matters, not name.
- Prefer unions of string literals and discriminated unions.
- Prefer `unknown` to `any`.
- `Omit`, `Pick`, `Partial` and `Record` derive request types from one model.

items.question: Why can't you use `instanceof` with a TypeScript interface?
items.answer: Interfaces are erased at compile time, so nothing exists at run time to check against.

items.question: What is the difference between `any` and `unknown`?
items.answer: `any` disables checking. `unknown` accepts anything but must be narrowed before use, so it stays safe.

items.question: Why prefer a discriminated union over `isLoading`, `error` and `data` fields?
items.answer: Three independent fields allow nonsense combinations such as loading with an error. A union allows only the real states, and the compiler checks each case.
